rows.note: This is the all-purpose construction for moving or passing across, above, or over an obstacle.

example.english: We’ll walk over the bridge first.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 haang4 gwo3 tiu4 kiu4 sin1

rows.note: Use this all-purpose movement construction when something crosses, flies over, or jumps over an obstacle.

example.english: We jumped over the puddle and got there.
example.traditional: 我哋跳過條水坑就到喇。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 tiu3 gwo3 tiu4 seoi2 haang1 zau6 dou3 laa3

rows.note: Use this for something positioned above A or placed on top of A, including when it covers A.

example.english: The lamp is over the table.
example.jyutping: zaan2 dang1 hai2 zoeng1 toi2 soeng6 min6

rows.note: Use 反轉 when something overturns or is deliberately rotated to the opposite orientation.

example.english: Turn the photo over and have a look.
example.jyutping: nei5 zoeng1 zoeng1 soeng2 faan2 zyun3 tai2 haa5

rows.note: Use 多過 for exceeding a number or amount, and after a preference verb to compare two choices.

example.english: This coffee costs over fifty dollars.
example.jyutping: ni1 bui1 gaa3 fe1 do1 gwo3 ng5 sap6 man1

rows.note: Use this when an object is moved aside or away from its original position.

example.english: I moved the stool over so you could get through.
example.traditional: 我將張凳搬開，等你行過。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zoeng1 zoeng1 dang3 bun1 hoi1 dang2 nei5 haang4 gwo3

rows.note: Use this when a person or place is on the opposite side of A.

example.english: The bus stop is over on the other side of the shopping mall.
example.jyutping: baa1 si2 zaam6 hai2 soeng1 coeng4 deoi3 min6

rows.note: Use 轉過嚟 when someone changes allegiance or viewpoint and comes over to the speaker's side.

example.english: They originally supported the other side, but later came over to help us.
example.traditional: 佢本身支持對家，後尾轉過嚟幫我哋。
example.jyutping: keoi5 bun2 san1 zi1 ci4 deoi3 gaa1 hau6 mei5 zyun2 gwo3 lei4 bong1 ngo5 dei6
